svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it — A whole GitLab page gets a row of its own in a storyboard, at its real size
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: A whole GitLab page gets a row of its own in a storyboard, at its real size

g.text: Then a storyboard gives a whole GitLab page a full row at its real size and keeps shorter
A storyboard drawn by the real engine from four pictures: a short terminal capture, a whole GitLab page 1440 pixels
wide, a long output strip 960 pixels wide and a second terminal capture.
The page takes the full width of the board and keeps its real size, so its small text stays readable. Its long note
wraps at a comfortable width instead of running across the whole board.
The pictures around it share rows two by two. The 960 pixel strip is not a page, so it is shrunk into its half of the
row instead of taking a row of its own.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 1 steps · 1 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
